trust_decision.summary: A PDF supplied by an untrusted party must not make pypdf spend super-linear time or memory rebuilding document-graph structures: the /Outlines tree walk (_get_outline) and the /Do-referenced form-XObject walk for text extraction (_extract_text) must both be bounded by an entry counter and a depth counter, not only by node-identity cycle detection.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary is 'Possible long runtimes/large memory usage when retrieving outlines', so an engineer looks first at the public `outline` property (pypdf/_doc_common.py:864-870) and the `_get_outline` walker it calls.

fix_sites.module_kind: core document-model module (shared reader/writer base class)
recursive outline walker inside the document-model module
page / text-extraction module (the new _extract_text__xform helper is carved out of the /Do branch)

fix_sites.entry_point: PageObject.extract_xform_text (public lower-level API called directly on a form XObject)
fix_sites.module_kind: public lower-level API in the page module

fix_sites.entry_point: internal helper reached only from the two sites above (new _TraversalState dataclass)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about outline retrieval; form-XObject expansion is a separate text-extraction feature in another module that already has its own cycle guard (known_ids at pypdf/_page.py:1919-1926), so a solver can argue it is protected and out of scope for this advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The same sub-outline may legitimately be referenced by two parents and must be expanded under each of them: the per-branch `inner_visited = visited.copy()` is deliberate, and the pinned test tests/test_doc_common.py:611-627 asserts the shared 'Nested entry' appears under both parents. A fix that shares one visited set across branches, or treats a repeated node id as a cycle, silently drops the second copy. The XForm side has the analogous case: `known_ids.discard(xform_id)` in the finally block at pypdf/_page.py:1939-1940 deliberately allows the same form to be invoked repeatedly.

O6_input_shapes: outline tree: many entries across /Next siblings and subtrees (entry-count bound)
outline tree: DAG where several parents share one sub-outline, giving exponentially many traversal paths in a linear-sized file
page /Contents that invokes a form XObject which invokes its children twice per level (form-XObject DAG)
a form XObject used repeatedly by nested form resources rather than from page content, and a direct PageObject.extract_xform_text call on such a form

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PdfWriter.merge/append with the default import_outline=True walks the source /Outlines tree in _get_filtered_outline with only a shared visited cycle guard: no depth and no entry budget, so a deeply nested outline raises RecursionError and a very large one is walked unbounded.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the merge/import path, not outline retrieval; it clones only the pages the caller selected, and the shared visited set already stops cycles, so it looks handled.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, pypdf/_writer.py, ~2,200 lines from _doc_common.py:_get_outline; reached from public PdfWriter.append (pypdf/_writer.py:2627-2684) / PdfWriter.merge (pypdf/_writer.py:2686-2797)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PdfWriter.find_outline_item recurses /First and iterates /Next with no visited set and no budget at all, so a writer whose outline was cloned from a cyclic untrusted PDF (PdfWriter(clone_from=...), pinned test tests/test_doc_common.py:616) loops forever on a /Next cycle or recurses without bound on a /First cycle.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a bookmark lookup on the writer's own in-memory tree rather than a read path for untrusted input, and it returns as soon as it finds a match (exercised at tests/test_merger.py:116).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the first route, public PdfWriter method, one module and ~160 lines from _get_filtered_outline

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A visited set plus entry budget in _get_fonts_walk, which recurses /XObject and /Annots with no guard at all
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same DAG expansion shape as the form-XObject text path and the comment at pypdf/_page.py:1984 already says the layout-mode font logic is adapted from _extract_text, so a maintainer hardening form traversal would plausibly bound font enumeration in the same change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A depth/entry counter threaded through _get_filtered_outline, mirroring the reader-side budget
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The two walkers are near-identical copies of the same /First and /Next loop and are maintained together; a maintainer fixing the reader side would naturally copy the counter into the writer's import path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An entry-count budget on the /Names destination tree walk (_get_named_destinations), which already has a visited set but no counter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: _get_outline calls it at pypdf/_doc_common.py:892 to resolve item destinations, so a maintainer bounding outline retrieval could extend the same state object to the name-tree walk.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A visited set and depth counter in find_outline_item
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the third walker over the same /First-/Next structure in the codebase, and the recent cycle guard in TreeObject.insert_child (pypdf/generic/_data_structures.py:820-824) shows the project hardening these walks one at a time.

O9_family: resource exhaustion through unbounded or amplified traversal of a document object graph (CWE-405 asymmetric resource consumption/amplification, CWE-834 excessive iteration)

Note the outline tests at tests/test_doc_common.py:587-616 are marked enable_socket and download sample PDFs; the fix's own new tests build PDFs in memory and run offline.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Treat a repeated node id as a cycle in _get_outline by dropping `.copy()` and sharing one visited set (exactly what _writer._get_filtered_outline already does), which stops the amplification but silently drops legitimate shared sub-outlines, adds no counter, and leaves the _page.py form-XObject walk untouched.
